findings.title: services.yaml still teaches the retired 0.15 wind-sensitivity default
findings.claim: services.yaml set_thermal_parameters.wind_sensitivity_factor has example 0.15 and says '0.15 means 15% more heat loss per m/s' while const.DEFAULT_WIND_SENSITIVITY is 0.03 and const.py documents 0.15 as the replaced, physically implausible default.
findings.mechanism: The default was lowered from 0.15 to 0.03 (const.py comment); README, configuration.md and how-it-works.md were updated, services.yaml was not.

evidence.machine: 8-core Apple M1, 8 GB, macOS Darwin 25.6.0, Python 3.13.1, tests/hastub stub

perturbation.change: Set the services.yaml example to 0.03 and reword the description ('0.03 means 3 % more heat loss per m/s'); |example − default| goes to 0 and the row flips to true

findings.proposed_fix_scope: Two lines of services.yaml (example and description of wind_sensitivity_factor)

findings.title: Two services.yaml number selectors admit 0, which the registered schema rejects
findings.claim: services.yaml declares min 0.0 for inter_zone_heat_transfer and min 0 for window_area, but SERVICE_SCHEMA_SET_THERMAL_PARAMS binds both through _positive() with vol.Range(min=0.01), so the Developer Tools form offers a value the call refuses.
findings.mechanism: Selector metadata in services.yaml drifted from the voluptuous schema; configuration.md documents 0.01 for both, matching the schema.

evidence.unit: selector bounds rejected by the registered schema (of 39 number selectors)
evidence.machine: 8-core Apple M1, 8 GB, macOS Darwin 25.6.0, Python 3.13.1, tests/hastub stub

findings.instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.__init__:SERVICE_SCHEMA_SET_THERMAL_PARAMS, read from the service registry after heatpump_optimizer.__init__:async_setup_entry

perturbation.change: Raise the two selector minima in services.yaml to 0.01 (or let _positive accept 0 for these two keys): the count goes to 0

findings.metric_definition: Count of (service, field, min|max) where the services.yaml number selector bound fails the service's voluptuous schema
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Two selector min values in services.yaml

findings.title: The '6.7 degree-hours to zero' reference run quoted in README and how-it-works does not reproduce
findings.claim: README:486-487 and how-it-works.md:1237-1238 quote 6.7 -> 0 degree-hours as the reference run recorded in tests/rolling.py; re-executing that arm with the test's own run_rolling gives 9.634 -> 0.044, deterministically, on the audit box.
findings.mechanism: The figures are a comment in tests/rolling.py:452-453, not an assertion (the test asserts only breach_learned < breach_plain); the docs quote the comment as a fact, and closed-loop solver output is machine/BLAS-dependent (tools/audit/README.md).

evidence.unit: degree-hours below the comfort floor over 3 days, learner off -> on
evidence.machine: 8-core Apple M1, 8 GB, macOS Darwin 25.6.0, Python 3.13.1, numpy 2.5.2 (OpenBLAS), scipy 1.18.1, threads pinned to 1
evidence.contention_note: fan-out (load1 2.8-3.8); a deterministic degree-hour sum, two runs bit-identical (rolling_learning.out, rolling_learning_rerun.out); solver floats are machine-dependent so the fixture machine may give a third pair

findings.instrumented_symbol: tests/rolling.py:run_rolling driving heatpump_optimizer.coordinator:HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator with learn=True (heat-loss learner) against plant_error=1.35 and a 4.25 kW pump

perturbation.change: D6_PLANT_ERROR=1.0 PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python tools/audit/round2/D6/rolling_learning.py (the house is the model): breach_uncorrected goes to zero

findings.metric_definition: Sum over the 3-day closed loop of max(0, comfort floor − room) × DT, computed with tests/rolling.py floor_for, for the learner-off and learner-on arms

null_control.note: tools/audit/round2/D6/rolling_learning_null.out; the number is entirely the mechanism's

reproduction_steps: compare RESULT breach_uncorrected / breach_learned with README:486-487 (6.7 -> 0)
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Re-record the comment at tests/rolling.py:452-453 and the two documentation sentences from a current run, or state only the asserted property (as how-it-works.md:1247-1250 recommends)

findings.title: DISCLAIMER calls the savings baseline an always-on thermostat; the optimizer's baseline follows the comfort schedule
findings.claim: DISCLAIMER.md:71-72 says the baseline is 'a simulated always-on thermostat', but HeatPumpOptimizer._compute_baseline_power simulates a conventional thermostat following the per-step comfort schedule (so a night setback is not booked as savings); only the hot-water baseline is always-hot, which README:271 states correctly.
findings.mechanism: The space baseline was changed to track the comfort targets; README was updated, the disclaimer was not.

evidence.unit: documents (of README:271, DISCLAIMER:71-72) contradicting the optimizer's baseline docstring
evidence.machine: 8-core Apple M1, 8 GB, macOS Darwin 25.6.0, Python 3.13.1, tests/hastub stub

findings.instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.optimizer:HeatPumpOptimizer._compute_baseline_power (docstring, comfort-target tracking) and the always-hot DHW baseline block at optimizer.py:4786-4816

perturbation.change: Reword DISCLAIMER.md:71-72 to 'a simulated conventional thermostat following your comfort schedule, with the hot-water tank kept permanently hot': C305 flips to true

findings.metric_definition: Count of documents whose savings-baseline description contradicts optimizer._compute_baseline_power's docstring (space follows the schedule) plus the always-hot DHW baseline
